theory.intro: Skewness can be read from a **box plot** as well as from a histogram or dot plot. Compare the whisker lengths and the median's position inside the box to look for a tail stretching to one side.
facts: Consider the whole box plot. Whisker lengths, box-half widths and median position provide evidence about skew; one feature alone is not a universal rule.
Equal whiskers do not prove symmetry. If the median is much closer to $Q_1$ than to $Q_3$, the wider right-hand half of the box suggests positive skew; the reverse suggests negative skew.

When matching a histogram or dot plot to a box plot, compare the shape and check that the values are compatible. Matching skew alone does not establish that the displays represent the same data. A box plot cannot guarantee a detailed histogram shape or predict successive column heights.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$A$: The right whisker is longer, and the median is closer to the lower quartile. Both features suggest **positive skew**, with a tail stretching to the right.

$B$: The left whisker is longer, and the median is closer to the upper quartile. Both features suggest **negative skew**, with a tail stretching to the left.

$C$: The whiskers have equal lengths and the median is centred in the box. The distribution is **approximately symmetrical**.

Both whiskers have length $12$: $20-8=12$ and $52-40=12$.

The median is much closer to $Q_1$ than to $Q_3$. The left box half has width $24-20=4$, while the right box half has width $40-24=16$.

The wider right box half suggests **positive skew**. Equal whiskers alone do not establish symmetry.

The histogram has a tail stretching to the right. Box plot $A$ has a longer right whisker, consistent with **positive skew**.

With $19$ values, the median is the tenth value. There are $6$ values below $17$ and $12$ below $27$, so the median lies in the bin from $17$ to $27$. This agrees with $A$'s median of $21$ and rules out $B$'s median of $38$.

Compatibility can be checked using the dataset $8,9,10,11,12,13,18,19,20,21,22,23,28,29,30,31,38,39,48$. It gives the displayed frequencies and five-number summary $8,12,21,30,48$.

**Box plot $A$ could represent the data.**

Read the ordered values from the dots:
$2,2,3,3,4,4,4,5,6,6,8,10$.

The minimum is $2$ and the maximum is $10$. The median is $(4+4)/2=4$.

The lower six values have median $(3+3)/2=3$. The upper six values have median $(6+6)/2=6$.

The five-number summary is $2,3,4,6,10$, matching **box plot $A$**.

The dots have a tail stretching to the right. In $A$, the longer right whisker and wider right box half also suggest **positive skew**. Box plot $B$ has median $8$, so it cannot represent these dots.

The right whisker runs from $45$ to $60$, also a length of $15$.
The whiskers are equal and the median, $35$, is centred between $25$ and $45$.
Symmetrical.

The left whisker has length $16-6=10$ and the right whisker has length $60-30=30$.
The median, $22$, is slightly closer to $Q_1=16$ than to $Q_3=30$.
The longer right tail suggests a positively skewed distribution.

development.solution_text:
The left whisker runs from $5$ to $30$, a length of $25$. The right whisker runs from $40$ to $50$, a length of $10$.
The median, $35$, is centred in the box, but the much longer left whisker suggests a tail stretching to the left.
Negatively skewed.

The histogram has most values in the shorter-time bins and a tail stretching to the right.
Box plot $A$ has a short left whisker and a longer right whisker, consistent with this shape. Its values are also compatible: its minimum is $10$, its lower quartile $12$ lies in the first bin, its median $20$ lies in the second bin, its upper quartile $30$ lies in the third bin, and its maximum $50$ lies in the last bin.
For example, the data $10,10,11,11,12,13,14,16,18,20,22,24,26,28,30,36,40,46,50$ give the displayed bin frequencies and box plot $A$.
Box plot $B$ does not match: its median is $40$, but $12$ of the $19$ histogram values are below $25$, so the median must lie below $25$.
Box plot $A$.

The left whisker has length $36-8=28$, compared with $58-50=8$ on the right.
The median, $46$, is closer to $Q_3=50$ than to $Q_1=36$.
Both features suggest a tail stretching to the left.
Negatively skewed.

The whiskers both have length $2$, and the median, $20$, is centred between $Q_1=19$ and $Q_3=21$.
The box plot is balanced on both sides.
Symmetrical.

The left whisker runs from $10$ to $30$, a length of $20$.
The right whisker runs from $70$ to $90$, also a length of $20$.
The whiskers are equal and the median, $50$, is centred between $30$ and $70$.
Symmetrical.

The dot plot has many shorter times and a tail stretching to the right.
Its minimum is $5$ and its maximum is $13$. The middle two values are both $7$, so the median is $7$. The middle value of the lower nine values is $5$, and the middle value of the upper nine values is $9$.
The five-number summary is $5,5,7,9,13$, which agrees with box plot $A$. Its left whisker has zero length because the minimum equals $Q_1$; its right whisker stretches from $9$ to $13$.
Box plot $B$ has a median of $11$ and does not agree with the dot plot.
Box plot $A$.

The median, $25$, is centred in the box. The much longer right whisker suggests a tail stretching to the right.

The median, $35$, is closer to $Q_3=40$ than to $Q_1=25$: the box-half widths are $5$ on the right and $10$ on the left.
Both the longer left whisker and the wider left-hand half of the box support negative skew.
Negatively skewed.

The whiskers both have length $15$: $20-5=15$ on the left and $60-45=15$ on the right.
The median, $25$, is much closer to $Q_1=20$ than to $Q_3=45$. The right-hand half of the box has width $20$, compared with $5$ on the left.
The greater spread to the right of the median suggests positive skew. Equal whiskers alone do not establish symmetry.
